title: Fast quantum-state transfer in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains beyond the noninteracting regime
abstract: Shortcuts to adiabaticity have made topological edge-state transfer fast in the single-particle regime, but their extension to interacting systems is obstructed by nonlinear phase accumulation. We show that this obstruction can be removed in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains by making the next-nearest-neighbor shortcut hopping phase tunable. In the mean-field regime, this yields an exact nonlinear shortcut: one hopping quadrature keeps the state on the instantaneous dark-state trajectory, while the orthogonal quadrature cancels the interaction-induced self-phase modulation. The resulting protocol is nonperturbative in the mean-field interaction strength. When applied to the full Bose-Hubbard dynamics, the mean-field shortcut remains beneficial but saturates below unit fidelity, exposing genuinely many-body corrections beyond the product-state picture. We then optimize the transfer directly in the many-body Hilbert space and find that complex, phase-tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings recover near-perfect fidelity. Our results show that hopping phases are not merely a technical refinement, but a key control resource for fast and high-fidelity transport in interacting topological systems.
summary: This paper develops advanced optimal control protocols to achieve fast and high-fidelity quantum state transfer in interacting SSH chains. By introducing complex, phase-tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings, the authors overcome nonlinear self-phase modulation effects that limit simpler mean-field shortcuts. The results confirm that precise control over hopping phases is crucial for realizing robust transport in strongly correlated topological matter.
main_problem: The primary goal is accelerating quantum-state transfer (QST) in topological systems while maintaining high fidelity, especially when moving beyond the noninteracting regime.
main_result: Complex, phase-tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings are identified as a key control resource that allows for near-perfect state transfer even in strongly interacting many-body regimes.
method: The study employs advanced optimal control theory, specifically Pontryagin Maximum Principle (PMP) optimization, applied to the Bose-Hubbard model dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains, extended to include interactions via a time-dependent Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. The analysis progresses from single-particle approximations to full many-body Fock space optimization.
key_observables: Transfer Fidelity ($F$), end-site populations ($\langle\hat{n}angle$), and the required complex NNN coupling strengths ($ho_{R,n}(t), ho_{I,n}(t)$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($g$), particle number ($M$), and the ratio of hopping parameters ($\epsilon = |t_2/t_1|$).
main_assumptions: The analysis moves through approximations: single-particle $ightarrow$ mean-field product state $ightarrow$ full many-body Fock space optimization. The complex control approach is key to overcoming limitations in the mean-field picture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of SSH chains with topological interfaces, showing prescribed NN hoppings and the engineered time-dependent real ($ho_R$) and imaginary ($ho_I$) components of the NNN couplings used for control.
paper_structure: The paper builds logically by first establishing shortcuts in the noninteracting regime, then extending this to an exact nonlinear shortcut within the mean-field approximation using complex hoppings. Finally, it validates these findings by performing full many-body optimization using PMP in the Fock space.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete demonstration of how engineering complex control fields (phase-tunable couplings) can overcome fundamental limitations imposed by interactions in topological quantum systems, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum devices.
